state.case_summary:
A 48-year-old man with a 12-year history of perianal fistula presented with recent mucinous discharge, pain, and perianal induration. One year earlier, he had undergone incision and drainage of a recurrent perianal abscess. 

On examination, there were two indurated, ulcerative lesions each 7 cm in diameter and three external fistula openings around the anus; there was no inguinal lymphadenopathy.

Upper endoscopy was unremarkable. Colonoscopy showed the internal fistula opening at the right side of the dentate line, with otherwise normal mucosa in the rectum and colon on digital and endoscopic examination.

Abdominopelvic CT and MRI demonstrated a well-defined mass at the level of the anorectal junction extending into the right ischiorectal fossa, with enlarged pelvic lymph nodes but no inguinal nodal or distant metastases.

Histological examination of a biopsy specimen from the indurated area revealed mucinous adenocarcinoma. A serum carcinoembryonic antigen level was within the normal range.
